reviews.proposed_text: They were two hundred in all, and they descended upon Ardis, which is the summit of Mount Hermon.[a] They called it Mount Hermon because they swore there and bound themselves together under a ban.[b]
proposed_footnotes: [a] Charles marks the clause about descending upon Ardis, the summit of Mount Hermon, as textually doubtful. The printed reading is retained here without reconstruction.
[b] “Ban” here means a binding curse associated with their oath. The passage connects the naming of Hermon with their oath and curse.
reviews.reason: The printed reading can responsibly be retained, but the draft fails to disclose Charles’s daggers around the Ardis/Mount Hermon clause. Its textual difficulty must be distinguished from the explanation of the oath and curse.

reviews.proposed_text: And these are the names of their angels: Semiazaz—he was their angel[a]—Arakibaremeel,[b] Kokabiel, Tamiel, Ramiel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Baraqiyel, Asael, Armaros, Baterel, Ananel, Zaqeel, Samsapeel, Saterel, Turel, Yomyael, and Arazial.[c]
proposed_footnotes: [a] The printed Geʿez says “their angels” and “their angel”; “their leaders” and “their leader” express the contextual sense.
[b] Charles records variant forms of names in this list. Arakibaremeel follows the combined printed form; it has not been divided into two names.
[c] Charles places daggers around Arazial, marking the name as textually doubtful. That printed form is retained rather than replaced with a name from a later English translation.
reviews.reason: Retain the printed list rather than reconstructing it from later English. Attach the notes to the verse, identify the name variants as an edition-level issue, and attribute Arazial’s daggers to Charles, not the OCR. The proposed name spellings are readable transliterations, not a reconstruction of original names.

reviews.proposed_text: These are their leaders of groups of ten.[a]
proposed_footnotes: [a] Or “their chiefs of tens.” Numbering this sentence as verse 8 is an editorial division; the sentence itself is present in the printed Geʿez text.
reviews.reason: The sentence is present on printed page 14 before chapter 7; the editorial verse boundary does not add source words. The English can stand, but the publication footnote should replace the internal OCR-check instruction. [unverified external reference omitted] supports the chiefs-of-tens sense as a semantic cross-check only.
